title: Peano arithmetic axioms
body:
Peano arithmetic axioms — an engine domain that can touch it: number_theory. Calibration: seals. Five axioms generating the natural numbers: zero is a number, every number has a successor, zero succeeds nothing, distinct numbers have distinct successors, and INDUCTION — if a property holds for zero and passes from n to n+1, it holds for all n. Induction is the engine; the rest is scaffolding.

THE SUBTLETY THAT MATTERS: in second-order form the axioms are categorical, pinning down exactly one structure. In FIRST-order form they are not — there exist non-standard models containing 'numbers' larger than every ordinary one. Arithmetic is harder to say than to do, and Gödel's theorems apply here first: this is the system his incompleteness result is about.

title: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic (unique factorization)
body:
Fundamental theorem of arithmetic (unique factorization) — an engine domain that can touch it: number_theory. Calibration: seals. Every integer greater than 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, up to order. Existence is easy; UNIQUENESS is the theorem, and it is what makes primes the atoms of arithmetic.

IT IS NOT AUTOMATIC, WHICH IS THE POINT. In the ring Z[√-5], 6 = 2·3 = (1+√-5)(1-√-5) — two genuinely different factorizations into irreducibles. Unique factorization is a property some number systems have and others lack, and recognising that gap is what built modern algebraic number theory. Practically: the difficulty of REVERSING a factorization, not of performing one, is what RSA rests on.

title: Fundamental theorem of algebra
body:
Fundamental theorem of algebra — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: partial — root counts verify; the existence proof is map-only. Every non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients has at least one complex root; by induction a degree-n polynomial has exactly n roots counted with multiplicity. The complex numbers are ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED — adding i to solve one equation, x²+1=0, unexpectedly solved every polynomial equation at once.

ITS NAME IS A MILD LIE: every proof is ultimately analytic or topological, resting on continuity or winding numbers rather than on algebra alone. A statement about roots turns out to be a statement about the shape of the plane.

title: Fundamental theorem of calculus
body:
Fundamental theorem of calculus — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: seals. Differentiation and integration are inverse operations. Part one: the derivative of the accumulated area under f is f itself. Part two: a definite integral can be evaluated by finding any antiderivative and subtracting its values at the endpoints.

WHY IT IS THE HINGE OF ANALYSIS: it converts a limit of infinitely many summed slivers — hard — into an antiderivative evaluated twice — easy. It also joins the LOCAL to the GLOBAL: a rate measured at each instant determines a total accumulated across an interval. That pattern recurs across the floor, in the divergence theorem, in Stokes' theorem, and in conservation laws generally.

title: Euclidean geometry & the parallel postulate
body:
Euclidean geometry & the parallel postulate — an engine domain that can touch it: geometry. Calibration: seals. Five postulates from which Euclid derived the plane geometry of the Elements (c. 300 BC), the model of deductive proof for twenty-three centuries. Four are immediately compelling. The fifth — through a point not on a line there is exactly one parallel — is wordier and less obvious, and generations tried to derive it from the other four.

THEY ALL FAILED, AND THE FAILURE WAS THE DISCOVERY. The fifth postulate is INDEPENDENT: it can be denied without contradiction, which is what produced non-Euclidean geometry and, eventually, the mathematics general relativity needed. Two thousand years of unsuccessful proof attempts were not wasted work; they were the measurement that located an axiom.

title: Non-Euclidean (hyperbolic / elliptic) geometry
body:
Non-Euclidean (hyperbolic / elliptic) geometry — an engine domain that can touch it: geometry. Calibration: partial — curvature relations verify; the choice of axioms is map-only. Deny Euclid's fifth postulate and two consistent geometries appear. HYPERBOLIC (Lobachevsky and Bolyai, 1820s-30s): infinitely many parallels through a point, triangle angles sum to LESS than 180°, negative curvature. ELLIPTIC (Riemann): no parallels at all, angles sum to MORE than 180°, positive curvature — the geometry on a sphere's surface, which is why long-haul flight paths look bent on a flat map.

The angle sum is a measurement, not a convention: it reveals the curvature of the space you are in from inside it, with no outside vantage point required. That is precisely what general relativity needs, and it is why a pure-mathematical rebellion against one axiom became the language of gravity ninety years later.

title: Pythagorean theorem
body:
Pythagorean theorem — an engine domain that can touch it: geometry. Calibration: seals. In a right triangle, a² + b² = c². Known in practice to Babylonian and Egyptian builders long before its Greek proof, and still the fastest way to lay a square corner with nothing but a knotted rope — the 3-4-5 triangle.

IT IS SECRETLY A STATEMENT ABOUT FLATNESS. The theorem is logically EQUIVALENT to the parallel postulate: it holds exactly when the space is flat, and fails measurably on a sphere or a saddle. Generalised, a²+b²=c² becomes the definition of distance in any inner-product space, which is why it reappears as the Euclidean norm in statistics, in least squares, and in the metric of spacetime with one sign flipped.

title: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
body:
Gödel's incompleteness theorems — an engine domain that can touch it: formal_logic. Calibration: map-only — a meta-theorem about systems, not a sealable computation. FIRST (1931): any consistent formal system strong enough to express arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove. SECOND: no such system can prove its own consistency using only its own rules.

THE METHOD IS THE MARVEL: Gödel encoded statements ABOUT the system as numbers INSIDE the system, then constructed a sentence asserting its own unprovability. Self-reference, made arithmetic.

STATE THE LIMIT OF THE LIMIT, because this theorem is more often misused than used. It does not say truth is relative, that mathematics is broken, or that minds beat machines. It says: no single formal system captures all arithmetic truth, and consistency must be argued from outside. For this project it is the keystone — a tool cannot fully validate itself, so any system claiming to be its own final authority is making a claim mathematics has already refuted.

subject: Gödel's incompleteness theorems

author: engine

title: Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory (ZFC)
body:
Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory (ZFC) — an engine domain that can touch it: formal_logic. Calibration: map-only — an axiomatic foundation, not a computation. Nine or so axioms about sets from which essentially all of modern mathematics can be built. Devised after the naive theory collapsed: Russell's paradox (1901) asked whether the set of all sets not containing themselves contains itself, and either answer contradicts.

TWO RESULTS DEFINE ITS CHARACTER. The AXIOM OF CHOICE is independent of the rest and yields consequences many find intolerable — Banach–Tarski, in which a ball is cut into finitely many pieces and reassembled into two identical balls. The CONTINUUM HYPOTHESIS is independent too: Gödel (1940) showed it cannot be disproved and Cohen (1963) that it cannot be proved. Some questions are not open pending more work; they are settled as UNDECIDABLE from these axioms, which is a different and stranger kind of answer.

title: Boolean algebra / propositional logic
body:
Boolean algebra / propositional logic — an engine domain that can touch it: formal_logic. Calibration: seals. Two values and three operations — AND, OR, NOT — with laws of their own (De Morgan's, distribution, double negation). Boole published it in 1847 as an attempt to put reasoning into algebra, with no application in view.

IT SAT UNUSED FOR NINETY YEARS. Claude Shannon's 1937 master's thesis observed that a relay is either open or closed, so a switching circuit IS a Boolean expression — and every digital computer since has been built on that identification. It is the clearest case on this floor of pure structure waiting decades for the physical system that would need it, and an argument for keeping mathematics that has no use yet.

title: Kolmogorov probability axioms
body:
Kolmogorov probability axioms — an engine domain that can touch it: probability. Calibration: seals. Three axioms (1933): probabilities are non-negative, the whole sample space has probability 1, and the probability of a disjoint union is the sum of the probabilities. That is the entire foundation.

THE MOVE THAT MADE IT RIGOROUS was recognising that a probability is a MEASURE normalised to total mass one — so all of measure theory applies at once, and questions about infinite sequences and continuous distributions stop being paradoxical. What the axioms deliberately do NOT settle is what a probability MEANS: long-run frequency, or degree of belief. The mathematics is identical either way and the interpretations differ; keeping that separation honest is why frequentist and Bayesian methods can share one calculus.

title: Bayes' theorem
body:
Bayes' theorem — an engine domain that can touch it: probability. Calibration: seals. P(H|E) = P(E|H)·P(H) / P(E). How to update a belief when evidence arrives: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior. A trivial rearrangement of conditional probability, and one of the most consequential.

THE BASE RATE IS WHERE INTUITION FAILS, AND IT FAILS EXPENSIVELY. A test 99% accurate for a disease affecting 1 in 10,000 returns, on a positive result, a roughly 1% chance the person is ill — because false positives from the vast healthy majority swamp the few true ones. Doctors, courts and juries get this wrong routinely; the prosecutor's fallacy is exactly the confusion of P(evidence|innocent) with P(innocent|evidence). This card is on the floor because the same inversion error is the commonest way a true fact produces a false conclusion.

title: Central limit theorem
body:
Central limit theorem — an engine domain that can touch it: statistics. Calibration: partial — sampling checks verify; the asymptotic claim is map-only. Add up many independent random quantities with finite variance and their sum tends to a NORMAL distribution, whatever the shape of the originals. This is why the bell curve appears everywhere: heights, measurement errors, sample means — anything that is a sum of many small independent contributions.

IT IS ALSO THE MOST OVER-APPLIED RESULT IN STATISTICS, and the conditions are the content. Independence and FINITE VARIANCE are required. Heavy-tailed processes — wealth, city sizes, market moves, earthquake energies — violate the variance condition, do not converge to a normal, and are precisely the domains where assuming a bell curve has caused the largest failures. When the tail is fat, the theorem does not apply and the model built on it will underestimate the extreme.

title: Law of large numbers
body:
Law of large numbers — an engine domain that can touch it: statistics. Calibration: partial — convergence checks verify; the limit statement is map-only. As a sample grows, its mean converges to the true mean. The weak law gives convergence in probability, the strong law almost-sure convergence.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY IS THE USEFUL PART. It does not promise that deviations get CORRECTED — a run of ten heads is not repaid by extra tails, it is diluted by later trials. That confusion is the gambler's fallacy, and the same error dressed up as sophistication is the belief that a bad streak is 'due' to reverse. Convergence of the average is compatible with the absolute deviation growing without bound.

title: Null-hypothesis significance testing (Fisher / Neyman–Pearson)
body:
Null-hypothesis significance testing (Fisher / Neyman–Pearson) — an engine domain that can touch it: statistics. Calibration: seals — a p-value recomputes exactly. Assume the null hypothesis, compute the probability of data at least this extreme, and reject the null if that probability is small.

THE p-VALUE IS P(DATA | NULL). It is NOT the probability that the null is true, and it is not the probability the finding will replicate. Nearly every misuse in the literature is that one inversion — the same error Bayes' theorem exists to prevent.

The threshold of 0.05 is a convention Fisher suggested, not a fact about nature, and the replication crisis is what happens when a convention becomes a gate: p-hacking, optional stopping, and testing many hypotheses while reporting one. This card is on the floor as a warning, not a tool: it is the most widely used and most widely misread procedure in science.

title: Graph theory (Euler, connectivity)
body:
Graph theory (Euler, connectivity) — an engine domain that can touch it: combinatorics. Calibration: seals. Dots and lines — vertices and edges — and everything that follows from which dots are joined. Euler founded it in 1736 by proving that the seven bridges of Königsberg could not all be walked exactly once: such a walk exists only if zero or two vertices have odd degree, and Königsberg had four.

THE MOVE WORTH COPYING is that Euler discarded distances, shapes and the map entirely, keeping only what touches what. Stripping a problem to its connection structure is what makes one theory serve road networks, molecules, epidemics, citations and this corpus alike — a keeping of cards joined by relations IS a graph, and its connectivity, components and degree distribution are measurable facts about the library rather than metaphors.

title: Combinatorial enumeration (permutations, combinations, binomial)
body:
Combinatorial enumeration (permutations, combinations, binomial) — an engine domain that can touch it: combinatorics. Calibration: seals. Counting arrangements without listing them. Permutations when order matters (n!/(n-k)!), combinations when it does not (n choose k), and the binomial coefficients that assemble into Pascal's triangle.

IT IS THE ARITHMETIC UNDERNEATH PROBABILITY: every probability computed by 'favourable over total' is two counting problems in a trench coat. It is also where intuition about scale breaks — 52! ways to shuffle a deck is around 8×10⁶⁷, so a genuinely shuffled deck has, with near-certainty, never existed before in the history of the world. Combinatorial explosion is why exhaustive search fails, which is exactly the pressure that produced computational complexity theory.

title: Linear algebra (vector spaces, eigenvalues)
body:
Linear algebra (vector spaces, eigenvalues) — an engine domain that can touch it: linear_algebra. Calibration: seals. Vectors, the linear maps between them, and matrices as those maps written down. The central objects are EIGENVECTORS — directions a transformation leaves pointing the same way, merely stretched by an eigenvalue.

FINDING THE INVARIANT DIRECTIONS IS THE WHOLE GAME, and it is why this card touches so much of the floor. Eigenvalues decide whether a control loop is stable, which vibration modes a structure has, the energy levels of an atom, the principal components of a dataset, and the ranking in PageRank. A hard problem written in the wrong basis becomes an easy one written in the eigenbasis; much of applied mathematics is the search for the coordinates in which a problem falls apart into independent pieces.

title: Shannon information theory (entropy, channel capacity)
body:
Shannon information theory (entropy, channel capacity) — an engine domain that can touch it: information_theory. Calibration: seals. H = -Σ p log p. Information is measured by how much UNCERTAINTY a message removes, so a predictable message carries little and a surprising one carries much. Shannon (1948) gave two theorems that bound engineering absolutely: source coding, which sets the floor for lossless compression at the entropy, and noisy-channel coding, which sets the capacity above which error-free transmission is impossible and below which it is achievable.

THE FUNCTIONAL IS THE SAME ONE THERMODYNAMICS USES for entropy, and that is not a pun: both count the number of microstates consistent with what is known. The identification runs deep enough that erasing a bit has a minimum thermodynamic cost (Landauer), joining information to physics through a shared equation.

subject: Shannon information theory

connections.evidence: a theory the sciences and math run on, calibrated

Shannon's H = -sum p log p and Boltzmann's S = k log W are the same functional, differing by the base of the logarithm and the constant k. Landauer's principle makes the identity physical: erasing one bit dissipates at least kT ln 2 of heat
entropy and channel capacity are defined over probability distributions on a message set

title: Church–Turing thesis / computability
body:
Church–Turing thesis / computability — an engine domain that can touch it: computer_science. Calibration: map-only — a thesis, not a theorem. Everything effectively computable is computable by a Turing machine. Church's lambda calculus, Turing's machines and Gödel's recursive functions were defined independently in the 1930s and proved equivalent, which is the evidence: three attempts to capture 'mechanical procedure' landed on the same class.

IT CANNOT BE PROVED, because 'effectively computable' is an informal notion — that is why it is a thesis. What IS proved is the boundary: the HALTING PROBLEM is undecidable. No program can determine, for every program and input, whether it terminates. Some questions are not merely unanswered but unanswerable by any machine, ever — the computational sibling of Gödel's result, arrived at by the same diagonal argument.

title: Special relativity
body:
Special relativity — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: partial — Lorentz and E = mc² relations verify; the postulates are map-only. Two postulates (Einstein, 1905): the laws of physics are identical in every inertial frame, and the speed of light in vacuum is the same for every observer regardless of the motion of source or observer. The second is the one that breaks intuition, and everything else follows from taking it literally.

CONSEQUENCES THAT COMPUTE: time dilation and length contraction by the Lorentz factor γ = 1/√(1-v²/c²); the relativity of simultaneity, so 'at the same time' is frame-dependent and not a fact about the world; and E = mc², mass as a form of energy.

THE REAL CONTENT IS AN INVARIANT. Space and time separately are observer-dependent, but the SPACETIME INTERVAL s² = (ct)² - x² - y² - z² is the same for everyone. That is the pattern this theory contributes to the floor: when observers disagree, look for the quantity they must agree on — the disagreement locates the invariant. Minkowski's reading (1908) is that space and time are one four-dimensional structure, which is what makes 'spacetime' a noun.

author: engine

title: General relativity
body:
General relativity — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: partial — specific relations verify; the field equations as a whole are map-only. Gravity is not a force but the CURVATURE OF SPACETIME. Einstein's equivalence principle (1907-1915): being in free fall is locally indistinguishable from floating in deep space, so gravity can be transformed away locally — which no real force permits. Wheeler's summary is exact: matter tells spacetime how to curve, spacetime tells matter how to move.

IT IS TESTED, REPEATEDLY AND AGAINST ALTERNATIVES: the anomalous precession of Mercury's perihelion (43 arcseconds per century, unexplained by Newton and predicted exactly); deflection of starlight by the Sun (Eddington, 1919); gravitational redshift; frame dragging; gravitational waves detected directly by LIGO in 2015; the Event Horizon Telescope image of M87* in 2019. GPS is the everyday case — satellite clocks run fast by about 38 microseconds a day from the two relativistic effects combined, and uncorrected the system would drift kilometres off in a day.

IT ALSO PREDICTS ITS OWN FAILURE. The equations produce singularities — points of infinite curvature at the centre of a black hole and at the start of the expansion — and Penrose and Hawking proved these are generic, not artefacts of symmetry. A theory that outputs infinities is telling you where it stops being the right description.

title: Quantum mechanics (Schrödinger equation)
body:
Quantum mechanics (Schrödinger equation) — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: partial — energy levels and specific relations verify; interpretation is map-only. A system is described by a state vector evolving smoothly and deterministically under the Schrödinger equation; what is NOT deterministic is what you see. The Born rule gives the probability of an outcome as |ψ|², and that step — from a superposition of possibilities to one observed result — has no agreed mechanism. This is the measurement problem, and it is honest to call it unsolved rather than interpreted away.

WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT is the predictive record: atomic spectra, chemical bonding, semiconductors, lasers and superconductivity all rest on it, and quantum electrodynamics is the most precisely tested theory in science, agreeing with the electron's magnetic moment to about twelve significant figures.

ENTANGLEMENT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE. Bell (1964) turned the question into an experiment: any theory with local hidden variables obeys an inequality that quantum mechanics violates. Aspect, Clauser and Zeilinger closed the loopholes over decades and took the 2022 Nobel for it. The world is not locally deterministic underneath — that is measured, not assumed. No information travels faster than light, because the correlations only become visible when the two records are brought together and compared.

title: Heliocentrism & Kepler's laws
body:
Heliocentrism & Kepler's laws — an engine domain that can touch it: astronomy. Calibration: seals — a deterministic verifier can CONFIRM or BREAK checkable claims drawn from it. Three laws, from Tycho Brahe's naked-eye positions worked by Kepler between 1609 and 1619: (1) orbits are ELLIPSES with the Sun at one focus, not circles; (2) the radius vector sweeps equal areas in equal times, so a body moves fastest at perihelion; (3) T² ∝ a³, the period squared as the semi-major axis cubed.

THE THIRD LAW IS THE ONE THAT SEALS. Give it a semi-major axis and it returns a period that can be checked against observation to many digits, which is why this card is not map-only. The first law is the one that cost the most: circles had been assumed for two thousand years, and Kepler abandoned them only because Mars' orbit missed a circular fit by eight arcminutes — an error he trusted because he trusted Brahe's instruments. Eight arcminutes overturned the sky.

Kepler DESCRIBED; Newton later EXPLAINED, deriving all three from the inverse-square law. That order matters: an accurate description that cannot say why is still knowledge, and waiting for the explanation would have cost eighty years.

title: Celestial mechanics / ephemeris prediction
body:
Celestial mechanics / ephemeris prediction — an engine domain that can touch it: ephemeris. Calibration: seals — a deterministic verifier can CONFIRM or BREAK checkable claims drawn from it. Computing where a body WILL BE: positions of Sun, Moon and planets, eclipse times, rise and set, tides, and the phase of the Moon on a given night. It is the oldest predictive science and still the sharpest test of one, because the prediction is falsified by anyone who looks up.

THE TWO-BODY PROBLEM CLOSES; THE THREE-BODY PROBLEM DOES NOT. Two masses have an exact solution. Three have no general closed form — Poincaré proved this in the 1890s, and in doing so found the sensitive dependence on initial conditions that became chaos theory. So ephemerides are computed by numerical integration, not solved, and they carry a HORIZON: the solar system is chaotic on roughly five-million-year timescales, and no increase in computing power removes that. Deterministic does not mean predictable.

This is field-useful and not merely academic: planting and harvest by season, navigation by star and by sun, tide tables for a coast, and the date of Easter are all ephemeris problems, and all of them work with no network and no power.

title: Big Bang cosmology & expansion (Hubble's law)
body:
Big Bang cosmology & expansion (Hubble's law) — an engine domain that can touch it: astronomy. Calibration: partial — the Hubble relation verifies; the origin claim is map-only (RESONANCE). v = H₀d: recession velocity proportional to distance, measured by Hubble in 1929 from redshifts and Cepheid distances. That relation computes and checks.

WHAT IS OBSERVED AND WHAT IS INFERRED ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS, and this card keeps them apart. Observed: redshift rising with distance; the cosmic microwave background at 2.725 K, found by Penzias and Wilson in 1964 while hunting a noise they took for pigeon droppings; and light-element abundances matching Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Inferred: that running the expansion backwards reaches a hot dense beginning. The inference is strong and it is still an extrapolation beyond any observation.

THE HONEST EDGES OF THE MODEL ARE PART OF THE MODEL: ~95% of the mass-energy budget is dark matter and dark energy, both named for what they do not do, and both unidentified. Expansion is space itself stretching, not galaxies flying through space — a distinction that changes what the recession velocity even means. A cosmology that states its unknowns is doing science; one that does not is doing something else.

title: Stellar nucleosynthesis & the HR diagram
body:
Stellar nucleosynthesis & the HR diagram — an engine domain that can touch it: astronomy. Calibration: partial — specific relations verify; the theory as a whole is not a sealable computation. Where the elements come from, and how stars are sorted. Hydrogen and helium (with a trace of lithium) date from the first minutes of the universe; everything heavier was made inside stars. Carbon, nitrogen and oxygen are fusion products; elements up to IRON are built by fusion that still releases energy; past iron, fusion consumes energy, so the heaviest elements require the neutron flux of a supernova or a neutron-star merger.

IRON IS THE HINGE, and it is a binding-energy fact, not an astronomical one: iron-56 sits at the peak of the binding-energy-per-nucleon curve, so it is the ash of every fusion chain. A star that has made an iron core has no fuel left that pays, and it collapses.

THE HR DIAGRAM is the sorting instrument: plot luminosity against temperature and stars fall on a main sequence with giants above and white dwarfs below, and a star's position gives its mass, age and fate. The claim that carries furthest is the plainest one — the calcium in a bone and the iron in blood were assembled inside a star that died.

title: Fixed-point theorems (Brouwer, Kakutani)
body:
Fixed-point theorems (Brouwer, Kakutani) — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: map-only — an existence proof, not a computation. Brouwer: any continuous map of a convex compact set into itself leaves at least one point unmoved. Kakutani extends this to set-valued maps.

THE HOMELY VERSION: stir a cup of coffee and at least one molecule ends where it began; crumple a map and lay it on the original and some point lies exactly over itself.

IT IS PURE TOPOLOGY DOING ECONOMIC AND PHYSICAL WORK. Nash's proof that an equilibrium exists in every finite game is a Kakutani argument, and von Neumann's minimax rests on Brouwer — which is why economics can assert an equilibrium EXISTS while being unable to say where it is. These theorems are non-constructive: they guarantee the point and give no method to find it, and that gap between existence and construction is itself a recurring feature of the floor.

title: Fourier analysis & signal processing
body:

Any well-behaved signal is a sum of sinusoids, and the transform moves freely between the time view and the frequency view of the same object. Fourier introduced it in 1822 to solve heat flow, and it was resisted as insufficiently rigorous.

NYQUIST–SHANNON sets the practical floor: sample at more than twice the highest frequency present and the original is recoverable exactly; sample slower and aliasing folds high frequencies down onto low ones irreversibly. Every digital recording ever made obeys this line.

title: Statistical learning theory (bias-variance, generalization)
body:
Statistical learning theory (bias-variance, generalization) — an engine domain that can touch it: statistics. Calibration: map-only — bounds are asymptotic and assumption-laden. Why fitting the data you have is not the same as predicting the data you do not. Error decomposes into BIAS, from a model too simple to capture the pattern, and VARIANCE, from a model so flexible it fits the noise — and reducing one typically raises the other.

A model that fits the training data perfectly has usually memorised it, which is why generalisation must be measured on data held back and never touched. VC dimension makes model capacity quantitative and yields bounds on the gap between training and true error.

THE NO-FREE-LUNCH THEOREM is the honest floor under all of it: averaged over ALL possible problems, every learning algorithm performs identically. Any method that works does so because its assumptions match the structure of the world it is applied to — there is no assumption-free learner, and a system that claims to be one is hiding its priors rather than lacking them.

How meaning is drawn from a text, and what makes one reading better than another. THE HERMENEUTICAL CIRCLE is its central finding: the parts are understood through the whole and the whole through the parts, so understanding is necessarily iterative — you arrive with a pre-understanding, the text corrects it, and you read again with the corrected one. THE SCHOOLS DISAGREE AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS KEPT: Alexandria (Origen) read allegorically for a spiritual sense beneath the letter, Antioch (Theodore, Chrysostom) held to the literal-historical sense; the Reformers held perspicuity and the grammatical-historical method — the text means what its author meant, in its language and its moment — against a reading secured by magisterium; the historical-critical school treats pre-understanding as contamination to be removed, while Gadamer answers that it is the very condition of understanding, and calls the goal a fusion of horizons. Ricoeur adds the hermeneutic of suspicion: ask what a text conceals as well as what it says. WHY IT BINDS HERE: every rule this library runs on is a hermeneutical commitment — original languages carry the authority, translation is a vehicle, a citation is not a proof, and authority is never silently upgraded by saving, repeating or hashing a claim. Kept as map-only: which reading is right is not a computation, and a tool that sealed an interpretation would be doing the reader's work and calling it verification.

title: Aperiodic tiling (Penrose, and the 2023 monotile)
body:
Two tile shapes plus local edge-matching rules that cover the plane completely and CANNOT repeat. Penrose (1974) gave two forms: P2, the kite and dart; P3, a thin rhombus (36°) and a fat one (72°). The rules are entirely local — each tile only constrains its immediate neighbours — yet they forbid any translational symmetry across the whole infinite plane.

TWO PROPERTIES CARRY THE WEIGHT. First, as a patch grows the ratio of fat tiles to thin converges to φ, the golden ratio, which is irrational — and an irrational ratio is precisely why no unit cell can ever close up and repeat. Second, every finite patch recurs infinitely often (repetitivity), so the tiling looks the same everywhere locally while never repeating globally. That is LONG-RANGE ORDER WITHOUT PERIODICITY, and it also exhibits five-fold symmetry, which the crystallographic restriction theorem proves impossible for any periodic lattice.

THE COUNT WAS NOT FUNDAMENTAL. In 2023 Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss found the 'hat', a SINGLE aperiodic monotile (using reflections), then 'Spectre', which is strictly chiral and needs none. So 'two tiles' was a bound on what had been imagined, not on the plane — a useful correction to keep on the card rather than in a footnote.

The honest calibration is map-only: specific relations here compute, but the classification of aperiodic tilings is not a sealable arithmetic claim.

title: Quasicrystals (forbidden symmetry in real matter)
body:
Matter that is ordered but not periodic. Dan Shechtman recorded an electron diffraction pattern from rapidly cooled Al-Mn on 8 April 1982 showing SHARP Bragg peaks with ten-fold symmetry — sharp peaks mean long-range order, and ten-fold symmetry is forbidden to any periodic lattice. Both at once was held to be impossible. He was told to go read a textbook and was asked to leave his research group; the result was published in 1984 and took the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2011.

THE RESOLUTION IS THE TILING. A quasicrystal is the physical realisation of an aperiodic tiling in three dimensions, and its diffraction pattern is the Fourier transform of that structure: a pure point spectrum — genuinely sharp peaks — arising from a structure with no repeating unit cell. Order and periodicity, which crystallography had treated as one idea, are two.

Quasicrystals were later found to occur naturally, in the Khatyrka meteorite (icosahedrite, reported 2009), so this is not only a laboratory artefact. The class is now standard: the International Union of Crystallography redefined 'crystal' in 1992 around discrete diffraction rather than around periodicity.

title: Girih tiles — quasi-periodic design in medieval Islamic architecture
body:
Girih are the polygonal tiles — decagon, pentagon, hexagon, bowtie, rhombus — carrying strapwork lines, used across medieval Islamic architecture. Peter Lu and Paul Steinhardt showed in Science (2007) that the tilework of the Darb-i Imam shrine at Isfahan (1453) forms a nearly perfect DECAGONAL QUASI-PERIODIC pattern, with the self-similar subdivision that generates it — roughly five centuries before Penrose described the mathematics.

THE METHOD IS THE POINT, AND IT IS AN ARCHITECTURAL ONE. At that scale the pattern cannot be laid out by straightedge and compass; the craftsmen worked by applying LOCAL tile rules and a subdivision recipe, and global quasi-periodic order followed without any global plan being drawn. The Topkapı Scroll records the design practice.

STATE THE LIMIT PLAINLY, because the claim is easy to overreach: this is not a proof that medieval architects possessed the modern theory, and the tilings are not perfect Penrose tilings — defects occur, and the interpretation has been contested. What is established is that the geometry was constructed and understood as a system, and that the same structure was reached by craft long before it was reached by proof.

title: Optimal packing & the honeycomb conjecture (Hales)
body:
The hexagonal grid is the most efficient way to divide a surface into regions of equal area with the LEAST TOTAL PERIMETER. Stated by Pappus of Alexandria around 300 AD as an observation about bees, it resisted proof for seventeen centuries; Thomas Hales proved it in 1999. The same author proved the Kepler conjecture on sphere packing (1998, formal verification completed 2014).

WHY A HEXAGON. Among regular polygons only the triangle, square and hexagon tile the plane, and of those the hexagon encloses the most area per unit of boundary — it is the closest a tile can get to a circle while still tiling without gaps. In a comb every wall is SHARED between two cells, so a hexagonal tiling costs exactly three walls per cell. That is the number to measure any cellular structure against.

THE CONTRAST WITH APERIODIC TILING IS THE USEFUL PART. A hexagonal comb is one tile, periodic, maximally efficient — and every cell is interchangeable, so the ARRANGEMENT carries no information. An aperiodic tiling pays slightly more and buys an arrangement that is itself information: infinitely many distinct patches, none repeating. Two answers to one question — how do you cover a plane — optimised for different things.

Calibration is `seals` because the geometric quantities here are computable: area, perimeter and the perimeter-to-area ratio of a regular polygon all verify directly.

title: Spectroscopy (how we know what a distant thing is made of)
body:
Spectroscopy (how we know what a distant thing is made of) — an engine domain that can touch it: optics. Calibration: seals — wavelengths, Doppler shifts and Wien's law all recompute and check. Split light into its wavelengths and a pattern of bright or dark lines appears. Each element produces a FIXED set of lines — a fingerprint that does not change with distance, temperature or motion, only its brightness and its position along the wavelength axis do.

THIS IS THE INSTRUMENT THAT MADE ASTRONOMY A PHYSICAL SCIENCE. Auguste Comte chose the chemical composition of stars in 1835 as his example of knowledge forever beyond reach; within about twenty-five years Kirchhoff and Bunsen were reading it off Fraunhofer's dark lines. Helium was found in the Sun's spectrum in 1868 before it was found on Earth, which is why it is named for helios.

THREE MEASUREMENTS COME OFF ONE SPECTRUM. Composition, from which lines are present. VELOCITY, from how far the whole pattern is Doppler-shifted — this is where redshift comes from, and therefore Hubble's law and the expansion. Temperature, from the shape of the continuum by Wien's displacement law. Nearly every astronomical claim on this floor secretly rests on this card, which is exactly why it was worth noticing that the corpus did not contain it.

The lines themselves are explained by quantum mechanics: an electron falling between allowed energy levels emits a photon of exactly that energy difference. Bohr's model gave the first quantitative account of the hydrogen series.

title: The electromagnetic spectrum & modulation (radio to gamma, one axis)
body:
The electromagnetic spectrum & modulation (radio to gamma, one axis) — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: seals — c = fλ, photon energy E = hf, and bandwidth relations all recompute and check. Radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma are ONE phenomenon at different frequencies, not seven phenomena. All travel at c; all obey c = fλ; all are solutions of Maxwell's equations. Visible light is about one octave of a spectrum spanning some twenty.

WHY THE BANDS LOOK DIFFERENT IS ABOUT ENERGY, NOT KIND: E = hf, so a gamma photon carries enough energy to break a molecule while a radio photon does not — the difference between ionising and non-ionising radiation is a number on one axis, not two categories.

MODULATION IS HOW INFORMATION RIDES A FREQUENCY. Amplitude modulation, the oldest form: s(t) = A[1 + μ·m(t)]·cos(2πf_c t), where f_c is the carrier, m(t) the message and μ ≤ 1 the modulation index. Multiplying two sinusoids produces sum and difference frequencies, so the spectrum of an AM signal is the carrier plus two mirror SIDEBANDS at f_c ± f_m — which is why a broadcast channel is twice the highest audio frequency (10 kHz channels for ~5 kHz audio).

AM'S TRADE IS THE INTERESTING PART. The carrier holds roughly two thirds of the transmitted power and carries NO information, which is grossly inefficient for the transmitter. It buys one thing: demodulation by ENVELOPE DETECTION — a diode and an RC network follow the outline of the wave, with no local oscillator, no phase lock and no clock recovery. That is why a crystal set (antenna, tuned coil, diode, earpiece) needs no battery at all: it runs on energy harvested from the wave itself. AM spends transmitter cost to make receivers nearly free and hard to switch off.

THE SAME AXIS READ THE OTHER WAY IS ASTRONOMY. A radio receiver tunes one frequency and rejects the rest; a spectrometer does exactly that across light. We modulate a carrier to impose information on it; a star's atmosphere modulates the continuum by absorbing at fixed frequencies, and spectroscopy reads that. AM sidebands and the Doppler broadening of a spectral line are the same mathematics on the same axis.

title: Spacetime & the quantum-gravity problem (where physics ends)
body:
Spacetime & the quantum-gravity problem (where physics ends) — an engine domain that can touch it: physics. Calibration: map-only — the Planck quantities compute, but there is no accepted theory here to seal, and saying so IS the content of this card.

TWO THEORIES, EACH SUPERBLY CONFIRMED, THAT CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT. General relativity treats spacetime as smooth, dynamical, and curved by mass-energy. Quantum field theory treats fields as quantised and probabilistic on a FIXED background spacetime. Each is verified to extraordinary precision in its own regime, and their assumptions contradict one another where both must apply: inside a black hole, and at the first instant of the expansion.

THE FAILURE IS TECHNICAL AND SPECIFIC, not a matter of taste. Quantising gravity the way the other forces were quantised produces a NON-RENORMALIZABLE theory: the infinities cannot be absorbed into finitely many measured constants, so the method that succeeded for electromagnetism and the nuclear forces fails here. The scale where the conflict becomes unavoidable is Planck's: l_P = √(ħG/c³) ≈ 1.6×10⁻³⁵ m, some twenty orders of magnitude below anything a collider probes.

TWO SHARP SYMPTOMS. Singularities: general relativity outputs infinite curvature, and Penrose and Hawking proved these are generic. The black hole information paradox: Hawking radiation appears thermal, so information that fell in seems destroyed — which quantum mechanics forbids, since its evolution is unitary and reversible.

CANDIDATES EXIST AND NONE IS CONFIRMED: string theory, loop quantum gravity, causal set theory, asymptotic safety. None has made a tested prediction distinguishing it from the others. This card is deliberately map-only and deliberately present: a floor that cannot say where it ends is an idol, and this is the edge — the two best-tested descriptions of reality do not fit together, and nobody yet knows why.

title: Liebig's law of the minimum (what actually limits growth)
body:
Liebig's law of the minimum (what actually limits growth) — an engine domain that can touch it: soil_science. Calibration: seals — nutrient ratios and deficiency thresholds compute. Growth is limited by the SCARCEST necessary resource, not by the total amount of resources available. Justus von Liebig's image (1840) is a barrel made of staves of different heights: it holds water only to the shortest stave, and lengthening any other stave adds nothing.

THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE WHOLE VALUE. A field short of phosphorus does not respond to more nitrogen; the money spent on nitrogen is wasted until phosphorus is fixed. Test first, then correct the deficit — which is why a soil test is the cheapest input a farmer ever buys. The primary macronutrients are nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (N-P-K, the three numbers on every fertiliser bag), with calcium, magnesium and sulphur behind them and micronutrients such as zinc, boron and iron behind those.

THE PATTERN GENERALISES far beyond soil: a system's throughput is set by its binding constraint, and effort spent anywhere else is absorbed without effect. That is the same shape as the bottleneck in a production line and the rate-determining step in a reaction.

title: Haber–Bosch nitrogen fixation (bread from air)
body:
Haber–Bosch nitrogen fixation (bread from air) — an engine domain that can touch it: chemistry. Calibration: seals — stoichiometry, yield and equilibrium shifts compute. N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, run at roughly 400-500°C and 150-300 atmospheres over an iron catalyst. Fritz Haber found the conditions (1909); Carl Bosch made them work at industrial scale (1913).

WHY THE BRUTAL CONDITIONS: the nitrogen triple bond is one of the strongest in chemistry, so the reaction is slow. Heat speeds it but, being exothermic, heat also shifts the equilibrium BACKWARD by Le Chatelier's principle — so the process runs at a deliberately compromised temperature and recovers the loss with enormous pressure and catalysis. It is the textbook case of engineering against an equilibrium rather than with it.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS DEMOGRAPHIC. Before this, usable nitrogen came from manure, legumes, and mined guano and nitrate; the supply was hard-capped. Roughly half the nitrogen atoms in a living human body today passed through this process, and it is commonly credited with supporting about half the world's present population. It consumes on the order of 1-2% of world energy.

IT IS ALSO DUAL-USE AND THE CARD SAYS SO: fixed nitrogen makes fertiliser and it makes explosives, and the same chemistry sustained the German war effort after 1914. Haber directed chemical-weapons work in that war. The runoff cost is real too — nitrate leaching, algal blooms and coastal dead zones. A technology can feed billions and poison estuaries with the same molecule.

title: The Green Revolution (Borlaug, semi-dwarf breeding)
body:
The Green Revolution (Borlaug, semi-dwarf breeding) — an engine domain that can touch it: agriculture. Calibration: map-only — yields are historical measurements, not a sealable computation. Norman Borlaug bred wheat that was disease-resistant, photoperiod-insensitive and — the decisive trait — SEMI-DWARF.

THE DWARFING IS THE INSIGHT, AND IT IS MECHANICAL. Fertilising a traditional tall wheat makes it grow tall and fall over under the weight of its own grain, so the extra nitrogen is lost to lodging. A short stiff stalk can carry a heavy head, so it converts fertiliser into grain instead of straw. Semi-dwarf varieties are what make Haber–Bosch nitrogen worth applying; neither achieves much without the other.

Mexico became wheat self-sufficient by 1956; India and Pakistan roughly doubled output in the late 1960s against confident predictions of mass famine. Borlaug took the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 and is often credited with averting a billion deaths.

THE COSTS ARE PART OF THE RECORD. The package requires fertiliser, irrigation and often pesticide, so it favours farmers who can buy inputs and can deepen inequality; monoculture narrows the genetic base and raises epidemic risk; and irrigation has drawn down aquifers. This card is map-only because 'was it worth it' is not a computation — but the yields, and the costs, are both measured.

title: Crop rotation & biological nitrogen fixation (the low-input path)
body:
Crop rotation & biological nitrogen fixation (the low-input path) — an engine domain that can touch it: agriculture. Calibration: map-only — rotation effects are empirical; nutrient budgets compute. Legumes — beans, peas, clover, lentils, groundnuts — host Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules, and those bacteria break the atmospheric nitrogen triple bond at ordinary soil temperature using the nitrogenase enzyme. What Haber–Bosch needs 400°C and 200 atmospheres to do, a root nodule does in a field, for free.

THE NORFOLK FOUR-COURSE (wheat, turnips, barley, clover) spread in 18th-century Britain and eliminated the fallow year: the clover restored nitrogen while feeding livestock, whose manure returned more. Rotation also breaks pest and disease cycles, since a pathogen specialised on one crop starves when the field changes.

THIS IS THE CARD THAT MATTERS MOST TO A FARMER WITH NO CASH. The Green Revolution package assumes purchased inputs. Rotation, intercropping and cover crops buy fertility with knowledge and labour instead of money, and they are available to a smallholder with no supply chain, no credit and no fuel. Lower ceiling than industrial nitrogen, far lower floor of dependency — and the two can be combined rather than chosen between.

title: Vaccination & immune memory (Jenner to eradication)
body:
Vaccination & immune memory (Jenner to eradication) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: map-only — herd-immunity thresholds compute; efficacy is empirical. Show the immune system a harmless likeness of a pathogen and it remembers, so the real encounter meets a defence already prepared. Edward Jenner (1796) observed that milkmaids who caught cowpox did not get smallpox, and deliberately inoculated with the milder disease — vacca is Latin for cow, which is where the word comes from.

THE MECHANISM, FOUND LATER, IS ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY: B and T cells that recognise a specific antigen proliferate, and a subset persists for years as MEMORY cells, so the second response is faster and stronger than the first. This is the immune system learning from a sample — the same shape as any system that generalises from examples.

SMALLPOX IS THE PROOF: declared eradicated in 1980, the only human disease ever eliminated from the world. Rinderpest followed in cattle.

HERD IMMUNITY IS A COMPUTATION, not an opinion: the fraction that must be immune to stop sustained transmission is about 1 - 1/R₀, so a disease with R₀ = 12 like measles needs roughly 92% coverage and one with R₀ = 3 needs about 67%. That threshold is why coverage gaps matter to people who cannot be vaccinated — infants, the immunosuppressed — and it is arithmetic rather than exhortation.

title: Antisepsis & handwashing (Semmelweis, Lister)
body:
Antisepsis & handwashing (Semmelweis, Lister) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: map-only — the effect sizes are historical measurements. Ignaz Semmelweis noticed in 1847 that the Vienna maternity ward staffed by doctors killed mothers at roughly three times the rate of the ward staffed by midwives. The doctors came from autopsies. He ordered handwashing in chlorinated lime, and mortality on that ward fell from about 18% to around 2%.

HE WAS REJECTED, and the reason is worth keeping: he had a decisive measurement and no mechanism, germ theory being twenty years away, and his claim implied that respectable physicians were killing their patients. He was dismissed, deteriorated, and died in an asylum in 1865. Joseph Lister, working from Pasteur, introduced carbolic acid antisepsis in 1867 and was believed, because by then there was a theory to hang the fact on.

THIS IS THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE INTERVENTION IN MEDICINE and it still is: soap, clean water and the discipline to use them before touching a patient or food. It requires no supply chain beyond soap, which is exactly why it belongs in a field library.

The methodological lesson is on the card deliberately: a measured effect with no mechanism is still evidence, and demanding a mechanism before acting on a clear result cost thousands of lives here.

title: Antibiotics & antimicrobial resistance (Fleming's own warning)
body:
Antibiotics & antimicrobial resistance (Fleming's own warning) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: map-only — dosing computes (see pharmacokinetics); resistance dynamics are empirical. Alexander Fleming returned from holiday in 1928 to a contaminated culture plate on which a Penicillium mould had cleared a ring in the surrounding bacteria. He identified the cause and could not purify it; Howard Florey and Ernst Chain turned it into a usable drug in the early 1940s, and the three shared the 1945 Nobel.

RESISTANCE IS NOT MISUSE OF THE THEORY, IT IS THE THEORY. An antibiotic is a selection pressure: the susceptible die, any resistant variant survives and reproduces, and the population shifts. This is Darwinian evolution running on a timescale of days, observable in a hospital ward. Fleming said so in his own 1945 Nobel lecture, warning that under-dosing would breed resistant strains.

THE PRACTICE THAT FOLLOWS IS SPECIFIC: antibiotics do nothing against viruses, so taking them for a cold buys no benefit and pays the full cost in selection; and a course must be taken as prescribed, because stopping when symptoms ease leaves the hardiest survivors to repopulate. Routine use as a growth promoter in livestock is the largest single driver worldwide.

title: Sanitation, clean water & oral rehydration (Snow's pump handle)
body:
Sanitation, clean water & oral rehydration (Snow's pump handle) — an engine domain that can touch it: medicine. Calibration: seals — ORS composition and dilution compute exactly. In the 1854 Soho cholera outbreak John Snow mapped the deaths, found them clustered around the Broad Street pump, and had the handle removed. Cholera was waterborne, not carried on bad air — and he showed it with a map and a count, before anyone had seen the bacterium. This is the founding act of epidemiology: a spatial pattern in data can identify a cause that no microscope has yet resolved.

SEPARATING DRINKING WATER FROM SEWAGE has saved more lives than any drug ever invented. It is civil engineering doing medicine's work, and it is the reason the great cholera and typhoid epidemics ended in cities that built it.

ORAL REHYDRATION IS THE FIELD-LEVEL COMPANION AND IT COMPUTES. Cholera kills by dehydration, not by the organism itself, and the discovery that glucose drives sodium co-transport across the intestinal wall EVEN WHILE it is inflamed means fluid can be replaced by mouth. The WHO formulation is roughly one level teaspoon of salt and six of sugar in one litre of clean water — ingredients a household already has. Deployed from the 1970s, ORS cut cholera case fatality from around 30% to under 1% and is credited with tens of millions of children's lives. The Lancet called it potentially the most important medical advance of the century, and it costs pennies.

title: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law — how all electricity is made)
body:
Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law — how all electricity is made) — an engine domain that can touch it: electrical. Calibration: seals — EMF, turns ratio and flux relations compute. A CHANGING magnetic flux through a circuit induces a voltage: EMF = -dΦ/dt. Michael Faraday demonstrated it in 1831 with a coil, a magnet and a galvanometer.

THE WORD 'CHANGING' IS THE ENTIRE CONTENT. A stationary magnet in a coil induces nothing; motion or variation is required, which is why generators rotate and why transformers work only on alternating current. The minus sign is Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change that produced it, which is conservation of energy showing up as a sign — if it added instead of opposed, you could crank a generator and get free energy.

ESSENTIALLY ALL ELECTRICITY IN THE WORLD IS MADE BY THIS ONE EFFECT. Coal, gas, nuclear, hydro, wind and geothermal differ only in what spins the shaft; the shaft turns a conductor in a field and the field does the rest. Run it backwards and it is a motor. Wind two coils on one core and it is a transformer, which is what makes long-distance power transmission possible at all.

title: AC & the polyphase system (Tesla, and why the grid is alternating)
body:
AC & the polyphase system (Tesla, and why the grid is alternating) — an engine domain that can touch it: electrical. Calibration: seals — transmission loss, turns ratio and phase relations compute. Nikola Tesla's contribution is usually told as a personality contest and is actually an engineering argument that has a right answer.

TRANSMISSION LOSS IS I²R. Power delivered is V×I, so the same power can be sent at high voltage and low current or the reverse — and since loss goes as the SQUARE of current, raising voltage tenfold cuts losses a hundredfold. Only alternating current can be stepped up and down efficiently, by a transformer, which needs a changing flux to work. That is why Edison's DC scheme required a generating station every mile or so and why the grid is AC.

THE ROTATING MAGNETIC FIELD (1887) is the deeper idea: feed three coils spaced 120° apart with three currents 120° out of phase and the resulting field ROTATES with no moving contacts. That gives the induction motor — no brushes, no commutator, nothing to wear out — which is still the workhorse of nearly every pump, fan and machine tool in the world.

The Tesla coil is a resonant air-core transformer: two LC circuits tuned to the same frequency so energy transfers efficiently between them, which is the same resonance principle a radio receiver uses to select one station out of the spectrum.

title: Fluid mechanics (Bernoulli, Reynolds, Navier–Stokes)
body:
Fluid mechanics (Bernoulli, Reynolds, Navier–Stokes) — an engine domain that can touch it: hydrology. Calibration: seals — continuity, Bernoulli and Reynolds number compute directly. CONTINUITY first: what flows in must flow out, so narrowing a pipe speeds the flow. BERNOULLI second: along a streamline, pressure plus kinetic plus potential energy is constant, so where a fluid speeds up its pressure DROPS — which is a statement of energy conservation, not a special force.

REYNOLDS NUMBER decides the character of the flow: Re = ρvL/μ, the ratio of inertial to viscous forces. Below roughly 2,300 in a pipe the flow is LAMINAR, orderly and predictable; above about 4,000 it is TURBULENT, chaotic and mixing, with far higher drag and heat transfer. One dimensionless number tells you which world you are in, and it is why a small model in a wind tunnel can predict a full-size aircraft — match the Reynolds number and the physics matches.

NAVIER–STOKES is the full equation set, and whether smooth solutions always exist in three dimensions is an open Clay Millennium Problem. We design aircraft, pipelines and heart valves with equations whose basic mathematical behaviour is unproven — an honest thing for the floor to record.

title: Heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation)
body:
Heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) — an engine domain that can touch it: thermodynamics. Calibration: seals — Fourier's law, R-values and Stefan–Boltzmann all compute. Heat moves three ways and only three. CONDUCTION through touching matter, Fourier's law: rate ∝ area × temperature difference ÷ thickness. CONVECTION by bulk movement of a fluid, which is why a draught chills and why hot air rises. RADIATION as electromagnetic waves needing no medium at all, rising as the FOURTH POWER of absolute temperature (Stefan–Boltzmann) — which is why a fire warms your face across a room and why a clear night sky freezes a crop even in still air.

THE PRACTICAL READING IS DIRECT AND IT IS WHY THIS CARD BELONGS IN A FIELD LIBRARY. Insulation fights conduction, and its R-value is thickness over conductivity. Sealing gaps fights convection, and is usually cheaper per degree than adding insulation. Foil and light colours fight radiation. Thermal mass does not stop heat, it DELAYS it — a thick wall shifts the afternoon peak into the evening, which is the whole logic of adobe and stone building in hot dry climates.

All three run only from hot to cold on their own, which is the second law setting the direction.

title: The Carnot limit (the ceiling on every engine ever built)
body:
The Carnot limit (the ceiling on every engine ever built) — an engine domain that can touch it: thermodynamics. Calibration: seals — the efficiency bound computes from two temperatures. No heat engine operating between a hot reservoir at T_h and a cold one at T_c can exceed efficiency η = 1 - T_c/T_h, with temperatures in kelvin. Sadi Carnot published it in 1824, aged 28, before thermodynamics existed as a subject and while heat was still thought to be a fluid — and the result survived the theory it was built on.

IT IS A CEILING, NOT A TARGET, AND IT DEPENDS ONLY ON TEMPERATURES. Not on the working fluid, not on the design, not on the engineering budget. A steam plant with T_h ≈ 850 K and T_c ≈ 300 K cannot exceed about 65% no matter what is done to it, and real plants reach roughly 40%. This is why waste heat is not a design flaw to be engineered away but a requirement: an engine must DUMP heat to a cold sink to run at all.

THE STRUCTURAL LESSON generalises past engines. The bound comes from reversibility, and it says the useful work extractable from a temperature difference is capped by the RATIO of the temperatures. Raising the hot side helps more than cooling the cold side, which is why materials science — how hot a turbine blade can get without failing — is the real constraint on power generation.

title: Group theory & symmetry (the mathematics of what stays the same)
body:
Group theory & symmetry (the mathematics of what stays the same) — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: seals — group orders, subgroup structure and symmetry counts compute. A group is a set with one operation satisfying four rules: closure, associativity, an identity, and an inverse for every element. That is the whole definition, and it captures SYMMETRY — the collection of transformations that leave something unchanged.

Évariste Galois invented it before dying in a duel at twenty, to answer why no formula in radicals solves the general quintic: the answer is a statement about the symmetry group of the roots, not about anyone's cleverness with algebra. Some questions are closed by structure.

THIS CARD IS ON THE FLOOR BECAUSE THE FLOOR WAS ALREADY LEANING ON IT. Noether's theorem says every differentiable SYMMETRY of the action gives a conserved quantity — symmetries are groups, and that theorem is why conservation laws are consequences rather than coincidences. The crystallographic restriction theorem, which forbids five-fold symmetry to any periodic lattice and made quasicrystals shocking, is a group-theoretic result. The Standard Model is organised by its gauge groups. Error-correcting codes, Rubik's cube and molecular vibration modes are all the same mathematics.

title: Topology (what survives stretching)
body:
Topology (what survives stretching) — an engine domain that can touch it: mathematics. Calibration: map-only — specific invariants compute; the classification results are proofs, not computations. Geometry without distance: study only the properties preserved when a shape is deformed continuously without tearing or gluing. A coffee cup and a doughnut are the same object because each has exactly one hole; a sphere is different because it has none.

THE POINT IS TO FIND WHAT CANNOT BE DEFORMED AWAY. Connectedness, compactness, the number of holes (genus), and the Euler characteristic V - E + F, which is 2 for every convex polyhedron — cube, tetrahedron, football — because it is a property of the SPHERE they are all drawn on rather than of any one solid. An invariant that survives every allowed deformation is the strongest kind of fact about a space.

THIS CARD IS HERE BECAUSE THE FLOOR CITED IT WITHOUT HOLDING IT. The fixed-point theorems under Nash's equilibrium proof are topological, not algebraic — which is why economics can assert that an equilibrium EXISTS while being unable to compute it. The pure-point diffraction spectrum of an aperiodic tiling is a statement about a space. Graph theory is topology with the geometry thrown away entirely, which is what makes it apply to a corpus of linked cards.
